description:
FOUND s461ar (agent AR, round 18) by a probe taken while measuring #911, and
PRE-EXISTING on both emission paths.  Not caused by anything in that session.

perl's capture variables are DYNAMICALLY SCOPED to the enclosing BLOCK: a
match inside a sub or a bare block sets $1 there, and leaving the scope
RESTORES the outer value.  PCL's captures are plain globals, so the inner
match's value leaks out.  Probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl at 4d2c17e:

    'abcdef' =~ /(bcd)/;
    sub f { 'xyz' =~ /(y)/; return "in=$1" }
    my $r = f();
    print "$r out=$1\n";                  perl: in=y out=bcd    PCL: in=y out=y
    { 'pqr' =~ /(q)/; print "block-in=$1\n"; }
    print "block-out=$1\n";               perl: bcd             PCL: q

The AGREEING half is worth recording so nobody re-derives it: a successful
match with NO capture groups DOES clear $1 in both (`'xyz' =~ /y/` then $1 is
undef), and a FAILED match leaves it alone in both.  The divergence is purely
the scope restore.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN ROWS: it silently corrupts any test that calls a
reporting helper between a match and a read of $1 -- which is why
Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t's #873 helper carries a comment forbidding s/// inside it,
and why the #911 table there re-establishes its match at the TOP of the helper
rather than at the call site.  A future guard that does not know this will
write a row that passes for the wrong reason.

SHAPE OF A FIX (unmeasured, and the cost is the point): perl saves the capture
state on the scope stack.  PCL would have to bind the capture state around
every BLOCK that can contain a match -- every sub body, every bare block --
which is a per-scope save/restore on the hottest path there is.  Measure a
cheap version first: only save when the scope actually CONTAINS a match
(a compile-time fact the emitter already computes for other purposes), and
only the groups the pattern has.

BAR: the two probes above; op/pat and re/ companion legs (they are full of
match-in-helper shapes); the counting-loop bench rows unmoved.
subject: capture variables are not dynamically scoped: perl RESTORES $1 on block/sub exit, PCL does not
